title: Does a Shared Temperature Imply a Shared Angular Scale in Probabilistic Contrastive Learning?
abstract: arXiv:2609.38784v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In probabilistic contrastive learning, a shared temperature is commonly interpreted as a shared similarity scale, but this interpretation does not hold for high-dimensional distributional class representations. We study the exact von Mises-Fisher (vMF) probabilistic score used by ProCo when representation dimension and class concentration grow jointly. We prove that the score retains a class-dependent leading angular gain $g_c=A_c/\tau$, where $A_c$ is the mean resultant length. This gain enters Softmax competition, pairwise decision boundaries, and feature gradients. On real CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist representations, the theory accurately predicts boundary movements and local gradient changes under the full vMF score. translated_title: 概率对比学习中的共享温度意味着共享角度尺度吗？
translated_abstract: 在概率对比学习中，共享温度通常被解释为共享的相似度尺度，但这一解释对于高维分布类表示并不成立。我们研究了当表示维度与类集中度共同增长时，ProCo所使用的精确von Mises-Fisher（vMF）概率得分。我们证明该得分保留了一个依赖于类别的领先角度增益 $g_c=A_c/\tau$，其中 $A_c$ 为平均合成向量长度。该增益影响着Softmax竞争、成对决策边界以及特征梯度。在真实的CIFAR-LT、ImageNet-LT和iNaturalist表示上，该理论在完整vMF得分下准确预测了决策边界的移动和局部梯度的变化。类温度调整还会改变余弦零截距和有限维响应。我们构建了保持截距和纯角度的对照实验，以将领先增益与这些伴随效应分离。
tldr: 论文证明概率对比学习中的共享温度并不等于共享角度尺度，并揭示了vMF概率得分中存在依赖类别的领先角度增益，该增益主导着Softmax竞争、决策边界和特征梯度的行为。
